items.title: CVE-2026-133626
items.description:
FlowIntel contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its file-to-note conversion feature. When a user converts an attached CSV or JSON file into a case note, the application renders the data as a Markdown table by padding every row to the maximum column count. A crafted file with a small number of filled cells but a very large number of columns (or keys) causes the application to allocate a quadratic number of padded table cells, potentially exhausting a worker process in memory or CPU.

The same issue affects nested JSON values rendered inside table cells, where pretty-printed indentation further inflates the output size.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated user with access to a case in FlowIntel
- Ability to attach and convert a CSV or JSON file to a note

Impact:
- Denial of service: exhaustion of a worker process, potentially disrupting service for other users

items.title: CVE-2026-133622
items.description: A flaw was found in certmonger. This vulnerability allows a malicious certificate authority or an attacker positioned on an unencrypted network to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending oversized or deliberately slow responses. Certmonger fails to enforce size limits or transfer timeouts when downloading and buffering Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP) replies over HTTP. Consequently, an attacker can exhaust host memory, drive CPU usage to capacity, or cause certificate requests to hang indefinitely.

items.title: CVE-2026-99804
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference

io_wq_cancel_tw_create() inspects cb->func after calling
io_worker_cancel_cb(). For an existing worker, that call can drop the
last worker reference and wake io_worker_exit(). If the canceling task
is preempted, the worker can be unlinked and freed by kfree_rcu() before
the callback function is inspected. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free
read in this path.

Save whether the callback belongs to an unpublished continuation worker
while its reference is still held, then use the saved result for the
conditional free. This preserves the existing accounting and frees only
the worker allocated for the canceled continuation.

items.title: CVE-2026-99803
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/net: mask socket type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK in io_socket_bpf_populate()

When an IORING_OP_SOCKET request is prepared in io_socket_prep(),
sock->type retains creation flags such as SOCK_CLOEXEC and SOCK_NONBLOCK
until __sys_socket_file() masks them off with SOCK_TYPE_MASK during
execution.

However, io_socket_bpf_populate() copies sock->type into
bctx->socket.type without masking off ~SOCK_TYPE_MASK. As a result, a
cBPF filter inspecting bctx->socket.type against socket types such as
SOCK_DGRAM or SOCK_STREAM can be bypassed by ORing SOCK_CLOEXEC or
SOCK_NONBLOCK into the socket type.

Mask sock->type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK when populating bctx->socket.type.

io_uring/register: enforce per-task restrictions in io_uring_register_blind()

When io_uring_register(2) is invoked with fd == -1, it dispatches
directly to io_uring_register_blind() without checking
current->io_uring_restrict.

As a result, a task with per-task register restrictions installed via
IORING_REGISTER_RESTRICTIONS can still invoke blind registration opcodes
such as IORING_REGISTER_SEND_MSG_RING even when those opcodes are not in
the task's allowed register_op bitmap.

Check current->io_uring_restrict->register_op in
io_uring_register_blind() before dispatching blind registration opcodes.

This is due to the /nelio-content/v1/post/(?P<id>[\d]+)/items REST route registering the 'values' argument with no sanitize_callback, storing values['efiUrl'] raw to the _nelioefi_url post-meta via update_post_meta(), and then interpolating that stored value into a style attribute via generate_style_tag() with no esc_attr/esc_url before splicing it into the img tag emitted by the_post_thumbnail(). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

items.title: CVE-2026-126715
items.description: The Xagio SEO & AEO – AI SEO for Google Rankings & AI Visibility plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.0.51 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wp_kses_post filter applied at save time does not strip angle-bracket-free double-quote breakout payloads in shortcode attribute values, leaving injected event handlers intact in stored post content.

items.title: CVE-2026-126012
items.description: The Contact Form Email plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.72. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to view and delete all stored contact form submissions, create, rename, delete, and clone forms, alter plugin database tables, and persistently rewrite the reporting options to silently email a CSV of all submissions to an attacker-controlled address on every subsequent request. The nonce intended to authorize state-changing POST requests is minted into the same management page the attacker can already render, so it provides no effective authorization barrier against a Subscriber-level user.

items.title: CVE-2026-120508
items.description: The Charitable – Donation & Fundraising Platform (Donation Forms, Recurring Donations & Fundraising Campaigns) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'stripe_payment_method' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.15.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. items.description: The Toocheke Companion plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'meta[<meta_id>][value]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.39 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. items.title: CVE-2026-133577
items.description: A flaw was found in the Kuadrant WebAssembly (WASM) shim shipped in Red Hat Connectivity Link 1.5. items.title: CVE-2026-99795
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cxl/features: Ensure that count is set before access to ent[] __counted_by()

get_supported_features() assigns entries->num_features only after the
memcpy() loop that fills entries->ent[] has already run. Since ent[]
is __counted_by(num_features), the compiler's bounds instrumentation
sees a 0-length array during that loop and FORTIFY_SOURCE trips on
the memcpy. Set @num_features right after allocation, before any
write into ent[], so the bound is correct for the whole lifetime of
the array.

This was found via a fortify panic:

 kernel BUG at lib/string_helpers.c:1043!

items.title: CVE-2026-99794
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject signalling responses in invalid states

A peer can send configuration messages while an
incoming channel is in BT_CONNECT2, before the
security or deferred accept gate has completed. A
configuration response can then promote the channel
to BT_CONNECTED. Configuration responses can also
act on channels that are closing, and a late connection
response can move a disconnecting channel back to
BT_CONFIG.

Accept connection responses only while waiting in
BT_CONNECT. Answer configuration requests in
BT_CONNECT2, but defer our own request until
BT_CONFIG so configuration cannot complete before
the gate. Ignore configuration responses outside
BT_CONFIG and BT_CONNECTED, and only complete
configuration in BT_CONFIG.

items.title: CVE-2026-99793
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: Only accept connection responses to outstanding requests

An outgoing channel waits in BT_CONNECT until security
and the feature mask exchange complete, and only then
sends its connection request. A peer can answer it
before that with a connection response matching our
source CID. The channel then moves to BT_CONFIG,
completes configuration and becomes connected before
security has completed. If security then fails,
l2cap_security_cfm() leaves the connected channel
alone, so it stays up on a link that did not reach
the required security level.

A connection response with a zero source CID is
matched by identifier. Another channel can hold the
same identifier for a response it still has to send,
so the lookup can pick the wrong channel.

Only accept a connection response while our request
is outstanding

items.title: CVE-2026-99792
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb/server: prevent file publication after tree disconnect

TREE_DISCONNECT closes the tree's published file handles before marking and
removing the tree connection. A concurrent CREATE that already holds a tree
reference can therefore publish its file after the close pass. When CREATE
drops its reference, the tree can be freed while the published file still
points to it.

both new-open and durable-reconnect volatile ID publication with that state
transition. An opener is then either published in time for the close pass
or rejected after disconnect with STATUS_NETWORK_NAME_DELETED.

Keep a tree reference while a file carries its tree pointer. This protects
asynchronous users that can defer the file's final destruction past tree

items.title: CVE-2026-99791
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: improve dirent bounds checking in scrub and repair

LOLLM complains that we don't do enough bounds checking of the directory

items.title: CVE-2026-99790
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set

nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() calls svc_xprt_create_from_sa() once for each
requested listener and passes flags of 0, so every listener registers with
rpcbind on its own. A rpcbind that accepts the connection and never replies
therefore costs one timeout for each entry. With the cap of 1024 entries
the request can hold nfsd_mutex for about 34 minutes, which is roughly 17
times the hung-task threshold.

One failure is enough to know that the next call will not fare better.
Read svc_rpcb_failure_count() before the create loop, and pass
SVC_SOCK_ANONYMOUS for the rest of the request once the count moves.

1015-byte segments, writev() returned 1015 instead of 1025 and KASAN
reported an 8-byte read beyond the nine-element iovec allocation.

number. A descriptor with nonzero upper address bits can access a different
MSR from the one described by firmware.

descriptors in the paired counter path.

items.title: CVE-2026-99785
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

9p/trans_virtio: reject mount tags longer than NAME_MAX at probe

p9_virtio_probe() reads a 16-bit mount tag length (tag_len) from the
device config and kzalloc()s tag_len + 1 bytes for chan->tag with no
upper bound. A malicious or compromised host can present a tag of up to
65535 bytes; that tag is later copied into the single-page sysfs buffer
by p9_mount_tag_show() (memcpy(buf, chan->tag, tag_len + 1)), a
host-controlled out-of-bounds write of up to ~64 KiB past the PAGE_SIZE
attribute buffer.

Reject an overlong tag at probe time. A 9p mount tag is a name-like
identifier, so bound it by NAME_MAX (255): that limit is independent of
the sysfs/seq_file page size and is far above any legitimate mount tag,
which keeps p9_mount_tag_show() safe at the root without hard-coding a
seq_file implementation detail.

items.title: CVE-2026-99784
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

9p/xen: fix refcount leak in p9_xen_response() on wrong tag

p9_xen_response() looks up the request for an incoming reply with
p9_tag_lookup(), which takes a reference on the returned p9_req_t. When
the tag does not resolve to a request in REQ_STATUS_SENT, the function
warns and continues the loop without dropping that reference, permanently
leaking the p9_req_t and its msize buffers. The reply header, including
the tag, is supplied by the backend, so a malicious or buggy 9P backend
can leak kernel memory on every crafted response.

Drop the reference before continuing.

items.title: CVE-2026-99782
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: also disable endpoints on p9_usbg_close

The close function has to fully reverse the state change of 9p_create

that the usage of the endpoints is not active any more.

items.description:

net/9p/usbg: set client to Disconnected on usb9pfs_disable

items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: always reset completion when disconnecting

When some tx or rx transfers were pending while closing the connection,
the completion handler could catch one pending completion call. To
ensure a normal start when mounting again, we have to reset the
completion and flush any pending completions.

items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

endpoints and their usb_request objects were left active and
allocated across a host-driven disable. When the host later
reconfigures the device, enable_usb9pfs() calls alloc_requests() again
and unconditionally overwrites usb9pfs->in_req/out_req, permanently
leaking the previous allocations, while the endpoints themselves are
left enabled underneath the function's own idea of being disabled.

items.title: CVE-2026-99778
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: fix out_req buffer leak in disable_usb9pfs

usb9pfs->out_req is allocated with alloc_ep_req(), which also
allocates the request's data buffer (req->buf). disable_usb9pfs()
frees it with plain usb_ep_free_request(), which only frees the
usb_request structure itself and leaks req->buf on every close.

Use free_ep_req() instead, matching the allocator, as documented by
its own comment ("Requests allocated via alloc_ep_req() *must* be
freed by free_ep_req()").

items.title: CVE-2026-99777
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

disable) independent of whether a request was ever queued. If it runs
before the first usb9pfs_transmit(), it reads the leftover sentinel
value, type-confuses the struct f_usb9pfs pointer as a struct

items.title: CVE-2026-99776
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: clear stale client pointer on close

p9_usbg_close() tears down the client transport, but usb9pfs keeps
using usb9pfs->client from asynchronous TX and RX completion handlers.
A late completion can therefore dereference a client that has already
been freed during mount teardown.

Clear usb9pfs->client under usb9pfs->lock when closing the transport,
detach any pending TX request from in_req->context, and make the TX/RX
completion handlers bail out once the transport has been detached. This
keeps late completions from touching a freed or rebound p9_client.

items.title: CVE-2026-99775
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfrm: interface: validate the IP header on xmit

Packets injected into an xfrm interface (e.g. AF_PACKET on an xfrmi
device) reach the xfrm output path without IP header validation, but
xfrm4_transport_output() uses iph->ihl for __skb_pull() and memmove()
and expects the header to be valid.

vti_tunnel_xmit() already calls pskb_inet_may_pull() before handing
packets to the xfrm output path.  Do the same in xfrmi_xmit() and
perform the header checks ip_rcv_core()/ip6_rcv_core() do on entry
to the IP stack: reject wrong IP versions and malformed IPv4 header
lengths.

items.title: CVE-2026-99774
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfrm: espintcp: reorder operations within espintcp_init_sk

When enabled on a socket, espintcp sets the socket callbacks to its
own before it has finished setting up its context and published it as
icsk_ulp_data. Any one of those callbacks that gets called before will
dereference a NULL icsk_ulp_data.

Fix this by reording the operations, and add memory barriers to ensure
callers will have a struct espintcp_ctx available. Add a few
WRITE_ONCE/READ_ONCE too while we're there.

items.title: CVE-2026-99770
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/vc4: Publish the output fence outside of job_lock

job_lock is taken by the V3D interrupt handler, so nesting an IRQ-unsafe

items.title: CVE-2026-99769
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/vc4: Drop the BO reservations outside of job_lock

vc4_queue_submit() calls drm_exec_fini() with job_lock held and interrupts
disabled. Besides unlocking the reservations, drm_exec_fini() frees the
object array with kvfree(), which asks for preemptible task context or a
non-NMI interrupt, and may reach might_sleep() through vfree().

Considering that an array that exceeds a page can take the vmalloc
fallback, call drm_exec_fini() once job_lock is dropped. The reservations
are then held across the job kick, which is harmless as nothing in the
completion path takes a BO reservation.

Note that vc4_attach_fences() has to stay inside the critical section, as
it walks exec, which the job done worker is free to release as soon as
job_lock is dropped.

xfrm4: use a full socket for local errors

items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: aic79xx: Fix NULL pointer dereference in device reset

Since commit c67e63800446 ("scsi: aic79xx: Do not reference SCSI command
when resetting device") the device reset SCB has no SCSI command, but
ahd_linux_dev_reset() still sets its residual, and ahd_abort_scbs(), which
completes it, sets its status. Seen on an AIC-7902 when a failing disk
triggered a device reset, which killed the SCSI error handler:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000009c
  EIP: ahd_linux_dev_reset.cold+0xee/0x26e

Add NULL command checks to the accessors in aic79xx_osm.h. Also skip
autosense for an SCB without a command and complete it with ahd_done()
right away: the REQUEST SENSE path can clear SCB_DEVICE_RESET, after which
ahd_done() would dereference the missing command.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

9p/xen: validate the response size from the backend

p9_xen_response() takes the length of an incoming response from the ring
-- the first field of the 9p header, which the Xen transport reuses as
its framing header -- and uses it to advance the consumer index, but
never checks that it is at least the header size or no larger than the

items.description:

9p: don't decrement a server-owned zero nlink

A 9P2000.L server can report nlink=0 for a regular file that still

items.title: CVE-2026-99762
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: mcast: validate tracker padding before forwarding

A multicast tracker with an even number of destinations needs two
padding bytes after its destination list. batadv_mcast_forw_packet()
currently only checks that the count field and the addresses fit in
the tracker TVLV.

If an unpadded even tracker is compacted to an odd number of
destinations, batadv_mcast_forw_shrink_update_headers() includes those
missing padding bytes in the amount to remove. The subsequent memmove
can then write two bytes past the old packet tail. With no tailroom,
this corrupts skb_shared_info.

Include the required padding in the existing tracker length check.
This rejects the malformed tracker before either received or locally
generated packets can reach the compactor.

items.title: CVE-2026-99760
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: tt: ignore ROAM flag of received ADD changes

A received TT change (OGM diff or full table response) with the ROAM flag
but without DEL is handled by batadv_tt_global_add() like a ROAMING_ADV:

* a newly created global entry gets BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM and is
  therefore excluded from the global CRC. The sender has it in its local
  CRC and the receiver has to request the full table again
* batadv_tt_global_purge_local() removes the local entry of the
  receiver. The receiver's own client is considered as roamed to the sender
  and frames for it are rerouted

The ROAM flag only has a meaning together with DEL. Drop it on reception to
keep it from populating the global table with a temporary ROAMING entry
which is not part of the CRC - and therefore causing a CRC mismatch.

items.title: CVE-2026-99758
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sctp: account for chunk padding in sctp_init_cause()

sctp_init_cause() accepts a chunk when skb_tailroom() can hold the
cause header and the payload. sctp_addto_chunk() then writes 0-3
bytes of padding before that header so the chunk stays 4-byte
aligned. The check does not include the padding, and the following
skb_put() calls skb_over_panic() from softirq.

Count the padding sctp_addto_chunk() is about to write. The cause
length on the wire stays the header plus the payload.

Found by LLM inspection, triggered and tested the fix.

items.title: CVE-2026-99757
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

btrfs: sysfs: restore NOFS context on early return in btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type()

btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type() sets up a NOFS context with
memalloc_nofs_save() because kobject_add() performs GFP_KERNEL
allocations deep in its call chain, and the function may be called
while holding a transaction handle or a lock required for a
transaction commit, where reclaim could deadlock.

Every other return path of this function calls memalloc_nofs_restore()
except the early return taken when another thread has already created
the kobject for the same raid index (this can happen when restriping).
Taking that path leaves PF_MEMALLOC_NOFS set on the calling task, so
all subsequent memory allocations performed by that task remain
restricted to the NOFS scope, which may lead to unexpected allocation
failures or deadlocks

items.title: CVE-2026-99751
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bpf: Fix skb_pull() BUG in __bpf_redirect_neigh()

The issue:
This is a follow-up to the short link-layer header fixes from Eric.
After vlan pop_eth, a privileged SCHED_ACT BPF program can call
bpf_skb_change_head(skb, 1, 0) and then bpf_redirect_neigh().

__bpf_redirect_neigh() calls skb_pull(skb, sizeof(*ethh)) after checking
only that mac_header < network_header.  Nothing verifies that the MAC
header is long enough, that it is linear, or that the IP header the
redirect goes on to read is linear either.

A SCHED_ACT BPF program can do:

    bpf_skb_change_head(skb, 1, 0);
    bpf_redirect_neigh(lo, NULL, 0, 0);

after vlan pop_eth.  The skb then has mac_len == 1 and only one byte of
linear data; skb_pull(ETH_HLEN) trips the skb->len < skb->data_len BUG in
__skb_pull():

    kernel BUG at ./include/linux/skbuff.h:2839!
